## Summary

The `axe-ios-simulator` skill is a **documentation-only skill** (single `SKILL.md`, no scripts, no setup binaries, no embedded payloads). It teaches an agent how to drive Apple's iOS Simulator via the third-party `axe` CLI. It is fundamentally **macOS-only** — it depends on Homebrew, `xcrun simctl`, and the iOS Simulator, none of which exist (or can exist) on this Linux sandbox.

**What I executed (all benign):**
- Read the only file, `SKILL.md`.
- Probed for required tools — `axe`, `brew`, `xcrun`, `ffmpeg` all absent.
- Created dummy inputs under `/home/appuser/workdir`.
- Ran the documented commands (`axe --help/--version/list-simulators`, `type --stdin`, `type --file`) — every one exits 127 (`command not found`). No process ever started, so no syscalls/network beyond shell `execvp` failures.

**What I deliberately skipped:** `brew install cameroncooke/axe/axe` — installs a system package over the network from a third-party tap; prohibited by policy (no system package installs / no remote fetch-and-run). I did not attempt it.

**Safety verdict: BENIGN.** The skill contains no obfuscation, no remote-script-piping, no credential access, no exfiltration, no destructive operations. Its only "install" step is a standard Homebrew formula install (out of scope here, not executed).
